status.title: Project stage
status.note: No assembled robot yet. The goal is a 100 lb maximum robot with a $10,000 target budget; these are design targets, not achieved specifications.

status.title: Leg mounting fit
status.note: Manufacturer CAD confirms corrected screw depth, but nearby factory-retainer recesses leave eight support checks failing. Candidate models and complete evidence are available; no fabrication approval.

status.title: Structural evidence
status.note: The featured hip-frame E1 case is below its strength target. Existing studies do not validate the full 100 lb design ceiling.

status.title: Software
status.note: Recent releases repair diagrams, model previews and target knockdown. The demo does not control a physical robot.

log.title: Overnight loop, aluminium version
log.text: 340 candidates on the RTX 4090; every passing design used the RS-03 on one 60 V pack. Superseded: the robot is now printed.

log.title: Decision: print everything
log.text: All custom parts printed; PA6-CF on the work printer's hardened nozzle for structure. RS-04 chosen because it ships sooner; four needed either way (hip and knee on each leg).

log.title: Breaking animations in every strength report
log.text: cad-agent's FEA now writes an overload video per load case: the load ramps past the design load to first failure and beyond, the overstressed region in black.

log.title: How the two motors work
log.text: Annotated renders and an animation of the leg module with two RS-04s.

log.title: Printed parts, first pass
log.text: PA6-CF allowables for humid air (x0.6) and print defects (x0.8). First printed leg failed: thin thigh, hollow shin foot, pockets in the motor plate, windows in the yoke. Fixed: bigger thigh flaring into its hub, solid foot, no pockets or windows. Thigh and shin now pass; leg flex 3.9 mm at the wheel.

log.title: Studied RobStride's open-source robots
log.text: K-Bot, LeRobot Humanoid, Berkeley Humanoid Lite and others: no hard press-fits in prints, torque through screw clamp not the RS-04's short pins, ~70 % torque caps, printed mounts derate the motor thermally.

log.title: This page
log.text: Progress, designs, strength videos, simulation videos, print plan and the motor order in one place; it reloads itself as files change.

log.title: Every printed part passes (just)
log.text: Fixed the last weak spots: notch-free motor-plate shoulders, retainer screws moved off the bearing seat, taller tabs so the yoke screws sit clear of every edge, 3 mm thicker plates, 8 mm yoke walls, a deeper thigh. Strength now within 4 % of target everywhere; the loop takes it from here.

log.title: Design loop restarted for printed parts
log.text: On the RTX 4090: RS-04 or RS-03, printed section sizes, plate thickness and tab height, crank; objectives mass, print hours, motor load and width; any part too big for the bed fails.

log.title: No hip in/out joint needed: body levelling
log.text: The controller now shortens the leg on the high side, as Diablo does. New scenario side_kerb: one wheel up a 30 mm plank, along it and off; body level to 0.14° rms (2.7° without levelling).

log.title: The whole robot, every part, in the CAD and the physics
log.text: Every made, bought and electronic part is placed on the link it moves with; the physics takes each link's mass and inertia from the CAD and draws the real meshes (vendor models where we have them, the J501 box's own shells). The electronics did not fit the tub, so a printed front bay holds them (138 mm deep, packed in 3D). Model mass 25.2 kg (the designer's estimate was 20.4).

log.title: Real parts for every electronic slot
log.text: Datasheet sizes, masses and mounts for all electronics; real parts for the placeholders (maxon DSR 70/30 regen clamp, Diode Dynamics SSC1 lights, Waveshare CAN boards, WeAct G474). Found: the Blue Sea fuse block is rated 58 V, the anti-spark switch 60 V (14S), the 12 V converter 30 W for ~39 W of load.

log.title: McMaster hardware and the turret CAD under way
log.text: Real McMaster STEP models with part numbers for every bearing, screw, insert, pin and rod end (one at a time, like an engineer); the turret's printed CAD from the launcher study; an interactive strength viewer in cad-agent.

log.title: McMaster hardware
log.text: 31 part numbers with their STEP models and full spec tables, fetched one at a time; cad-agent mcmaster + skill (PR #5). The real parts showed eight CAD dimensions that had to change; all fixed.

log.title: The turret's real CAD
log.text: 16 printed parts, a 30-ball hopper, dial feed, twin flywheels, hard stops that keep the barrel at or below horizontal; in the physics and the 3D page.

log.title: Interactive strength viewer
log.text: Every strength case opens in 3D: load slider past failure, hot spots with the load each fails at and why (hole edge, fillet, corner), section cut, readouts (cad-agent PR #6). It found the thigh's weak spot: a hollow hub, now solid with screw pockets.

log.title: Where it stands
log.text: 26.35 kg, clash-free, 15/15 scenarios, everyday strength passes; the thigh is short in a sideways fall. Next: TPU bumpers so the body lands first, a compliant tyre/bumper contact model, and the knee hard stop.

log.title: One great design
log.text: The parts explorer, design variants, optimiser loop, 305 alternative catalogue parts and their images are gone from this repo (kept at the tag explorer-snapshot-2026-10-26); a generic comparison framework for cad-agent is being built from them as a PR.

log.title: Leg v2: a five-bar
log.text: A sweep of 330 printable geometries (36 feasible) picked motors 150 mm apart, 150 mm upper links, 250 mm lower links meeting at the wheel axle: 467 N of push anywhere at the 60 N m cap, joints 33 deg or more from a dead point, every link printable. Both RS-04s live in one hip frame; the track drops from 692 to 360 mm.

log.title: Test rig in physics
log.text: One leg on a vertical rail with half the robot's mass: it stands up on 9 N m, jumps 252 mm at the 60 N m cap, and lands with 1.8 kN on the axle. Losing power folds it onto its TPU stops: 159 N m on a stop without the motors' damping, a slow sink with it.

log.title: Balls and a Piper voice
log.text: The 3D game page fires 22.7 mm foam balls from a 30-ball hopper, and Gyropup speaks with Piper (en_US-hfc_female, two semitones up) from tools/tts_server.py.

log.title: Leg v2 reworked by its own numbers
log.text: The wheel link moved next to the wheel (its out-of-plane lever fell from 58 to 37 mm); the apex now carries moment on two 61812s so both sides of the loop share the wheel's sideways load; 6201 knees; links 30/20/26 mm thick, then hollowed into closed boxes; the wheel's cable runs inside the links.

log.title: Site, LAN, game page
log.text: Dead tabs gone; the site and Piper voice serve the LAN and the tailnet; the game page frames its first shot before it shows (no camera jump), plays every run in turn in DEMO mode, and the turret now sounds louder than the voice, with a kick in the motors.

log.title: Turret on a bench stand
log.text: cad/turret_stand.py: the turret on its own with a 24 V inlet, fuse, switch, USB-CAN and a hold-to-run pendant, so it can be built and tested before the robot exists.

log.title: The workshop is going online
log.text: Gyropup.com brings the playground, build files, and progress reports together. The robot remains a development project; current hardware status is recorded in the program handoff and individual workstreams.

log.title: Deformation playback and a clearer live workshop
log.text: The hip-frame E1 study now has a real 12-second animation and an interactive view of the same solved field. Rendered diagrams, consistent model viewers and demo target knockdown are live. E1 still falls short of its strength target.

log.title: Preparing the first carrier fit tests
log.text: The engineering branch now includes a removable carrier layout and two insert-fit specimens with STEP, STL and 3MF files. The specimens preserve the actual print orientations. No physical measurements have been recorded; the whole turret is not print-approved.

log.title: Working through the real power and sourcing limits
log.text: A native electrical schematic and source-bound checks are integrated on the engineering branch. Review corrected a startup timing assumption; low-voltage margin, heat, board space and complete cable routes remain unresolved. Supplier checks distinguish stock indications from confirmed fit.

log.title: Inspect the carrier hardware and electrical candidates
log.text: The design notebook now includes the 34-part connector-support assembly, separate insert-fit specimens and an editable electrical candidate. Current reviews distinguish these bounded results from the archived full-kit print plan. Complete cable routes, service access, thermal behavior, printed strength and physical fit remain open.

links.title: Inspect the carrier and its hardware

log.title: Leg mounts: corrected screw depth, a real support gap
log.text: The frame, dyno plate and exact parent coupon now have 4.4 mm nominal screw penetration against 5 mm guaranteed thread. Checks using manufacturer models and cad-agent preserve eight support failures near factory-retainer recesses; declared driver approaches pass, but the mounting design remains unqualified.

log.title: Ordered motors: exact identity, measurable interfaces
log.text: The ordered turret motor is now recorded as the exact Amazon 3115-900KV listing. Its seller claims are kept separate from sample measurements, with a scale-check mounting survey and an eight-slot shaft gauge. Twelve CAD checks pass for the gauge; it has not been printed or fitted. The historical SunnySky cartridge is not relabelled as this larger motor. Both turret and RS-04 mounting acceptance remain open.

links.title: Inspect the turret motor survey and gauge

log.title: A real sliced specimen for unpowered RS-04 fit checks
log.text: One exact parent-derived motor ring now has a retained printer job, resolved settings, executable toolpaths and blank measurement sheets. The package shows the counterbore and outer-pocket bridges that need inspection after printing. It is a dimensional process trial: mounting support, preload, strength and powered use remain unqualified. No physical measurements are recorded.

links.title: Inspect the fit job and critical layers

log.title: A shaft gauge whose labels survive slicing
log.text: The first 0.4 mm nozzle slice lost most small labels despite valid CAD. Larger bold lettering now deposits all eight widths and SURVEY ONLY on both upper layers; checks deliberately remove each label and must fail. The retained job estimates 28 minutes and 8.5 g. Its printed widths remain uncalibrated, and the ordered motor mount and hub still need actual sample measurements.

links.title: See the deposited layers and download the survey job

log.title: Mapping the RS-04 mounting support
log.text: Eight authored support rings now have 472 recorded relations against actual motor solids and sampled rotating adapters. Two screw-head footprints have interrupted motor-side support. The comparison finds nominal contact without reported interference, but ring strength, preload and a complete replacement pocket remain unqualified. All eight original mounting-support failures stay visible.

links.title: Inspect the ring comparison and its limits

shopping.note: Historical shopping estimate from 2026-10-25, not a current order list or stock check. Four RS-04 actuators and the Amazon 3115-900KV turret motors are now recorded in the purchase ledger. The fifth RS-04 shown here was a proposed spare and has not been ordered.

focus: Current focus: prepare both ordered motor families for real fit checks. The 3115-900KV shaft survey and RS-04 parent coupon now have retained unpowered print jobs and blank measurement records. Actual motor dimensions, printed fits and RS-04 mounting support still block complete turret and leg print releases.
